uxDefinition.narrative: VS Code implementation schematic after manual feedback: connections list above both New and Edit forms at every width, dedicated themed tab icon, and icon-only Add/Refresh/Previous/Next/Delete-or-Discard/Close buttons with accessible names and tooltips. The shared model and capability checks also back JetBrains; its native layout is unchanged by this VS Code correction. Valid v2 safe-read/driver metadata permits local draft editing even when workbench sessions are unavailable. Save/Test/Remove retain independent advertised-capability admission and daemon authorization. Live UI validation is assigned to the user after plugin installation; this schematic is not execution evidence. File sources put File path first, explain optional Label, and use a native Browse dialog. Persistent Save/Test guidance distinguishes missing inputs from disabled daemon capabilities; delayed picker results cannot replace an edited or hidden draft. User policy correction: the daemon enables connection management by default; pending release-audit evidence no longer controls runtime capabilities. Real authorization, registry recovery, signed revisions/tickets and session ownership still apply. Existing unavailable-state examples remain compatibility/recovery alternatives. File selection now uses an accessible icon-only file-open button for both primary data paths and database Schema Source paths; path reset buttons are not used as file selectors. The native selection targets the exact allowlisted field, and a schema-source selection populates its fixed format before validation. User-approved October 31 correction: datasource-specific local SVG badges appear in the icon-capable keyboard picker, list and edit view. Each row has its own Delete/Discard icon targeting its exact key and revision, including when a different draft is open. A fixed two-line bottom message section shows the latest registration status and retained count; clicking opens a modal with Previous/Next cycling and recovery controls. Safe history stays in workbench memory, retains at most 200 messages per selected repository, survives manager close/reopen and clears on repository switch or workbench disposal. No draft values, credentials or raw exception messages enter the history.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Both live clients keep session ownership above manager views: extension workbench or JetBrains Project. A lost reply reconciles the original operation; closing Settings/manager does not end temporary state. Per-action feature checks precede effect submission; unsupported Test does not block Save. Same-epoch recovery retains original tickets; no legacy mutation fallback.

componentDependencyDefinition.narrative: Native TypeScript and Kotlin consumers share protocol/scenario fixtures, not executable source. Only each workbench/project transport adapter reaches existing daemon owners. Deprecated insrc-ide is excluded. One owner per extension workbench or actual JetBrains Project; manager views do not own sessions. Legacy application gateway stays stateless. Runtime feature availability is enabled by default independently of historical release audit; the daemon owns exclusive fresh-root initialization and signed Saved state.
